children: Our Bureau Mumbai: Jindal Steel's consolidated profit increased 21% year-on-year to 771 crore in July-September, anchored by a 44% year-on-year surge in gross revenue to an all-time high of 19,448 crore. Both revenue and profit surpassed analysts' estimates during the second quarter of this financial year.

The company reported its earnings during market hours on Friday, and its shares closed at 1,012 apiece on the BSE, down 1.7% from the previous close. Consolidated steel production increased to 2.4 million tonnes during the quarter, up from 2 million tonnes a year ago, while sales rose to 2.38 million tonnes from 1.87 million tonnes. Adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) increased 33% year-on-year to 2,504 crore in July-September, while adjusted Ebitda on each tonne of steel stood at 10,529 per tonne during the quarter, up from 10,010 per tonne a year ago. The company sold a higher share of flat products in its overall sales mix and fewer thermo-mechanically treated rebars among its long products, boosting the average selling price, according to its statement.

title: Jindal Steel Net Jumps on Record Revenues
